subject: English
passage: Wheat was domesticated in the Middle East. Its form is no longer the same as the form of the wild plant it is descended from. Rice also ______ its wild ancestor. That ancestor plant had seeds that scattered easily. Early farmers in East Asia selectively cultivated the crop until it had seeds that remained on the plant.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of domesticated crops and their wild ancestors. As used in this context, 'varies from' means differs from or is different from. The text establishes a parallel structure: domesticated wheat's form 'is no longer the same as' its wild ancestor's form, and the word 'also' signals that rice has an identical relationship to its ancestor. The text then confirms this difference by explaining that wild rice had seeds that scattered easily, while domesticated rice was selectively cultivated to have seeds that remained on the plant—a clear variation from the ancestral form.
